items.text: Many of us grew up learning that humans have five senses: sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch - an idea dating back to the Ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that humans have five senses: sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch

level1.label: 同位语
level1.text: an idea dating back to the Ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle

level2.label: 后置定语
level2.text: dating back to the Ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle

items.text: But what if this list is incomplete?
A sense is anything that can give your body information about the outside world, and some of these don't neatly fit into the traditional five.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: anything that can give your body information about the outside world

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: that can give your body information about the outside world

items.text: Modern scientists estimate there may be up to 33 different senses.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: there may be up to 33 different senses

items.text: One sense that doesn't fit into one of the five boxes is proprioception.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: One sense that doesn't fit into one of the five boxes

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: that doesn't fit into one of the five boxes

items.text: This is the sense of where your body parts are in space.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: the sense of where your body parts are in space

level2.label: 同位语从句
level2.text: where your body parts are in space

items.text: Thanks to this sense, you can touch your nose with your eyes closed and walk around in the dark - you know where your legs are without looking.
Then there's interoception which helps you sense things inside your body, like hunger and an increased heart rate.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: interoception which helps you sense things inside your body

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: which helps you sense things inside your body

items.text: And don't take your sense of balance for granted.
Balance relies on fluid in your inner ear to help you stay upright - this is what's called vestibular perception.
And the traditional five senses might not be as simple as they seem.
Touch, the sense we associate with our hands and tactile sensations, also encompasses the sensation of pain, temperature and itch.

level1.label: 同位语
level1.text: the sense we associate with our hands and tactile sensations

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: the sensation of pain, temperature and itch

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: we associate with our hands and tactile sensations

items.text: To perceive the flavours in food and drink, you need a combination of taste, smell and touch to get the full experience - it's not all about the taste buds on your tongue!

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: To perceive the flavours in food and drink

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: a combination of taste, smell and touch

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: not all about the taste buds on your tongue

items.text: It is actually smell that contributes most of what we perceive as taste, so when a person suffers olfactory loss, they often can't enjoy food as much, according to a 2022 study published in Foods by Fjaeldstad and Smith.

level1.label: 定语从句
level1.text: that contributes most of what we perceive as taste

level1.label: 结果状语从句
level1.text: so when a person suffers olfactory loss, they often can't enjoy food as much

level2.label: 时间状语从句
level2.text: when a person suffers olfactory loss

items.text: Until recently, philosophers and scientists have studied each of the traditional five senses in isolation, but researchers at the University of London's Centre for the Study of the Senses have more of a multisensory approach - the senses are all working together to create an overall picture.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: each of the traditional five senses

items.text: In their 'Rethinking the Senses' project, they found that our perception of salt, sweet and sour flavours is reduced when there is white noise, but our perception of umami is not.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that our perception of salt, sweet and sour flavours is reduced when there is white noise

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: our perception of umami is not

items.text: This means that sound can enhance flavour, and that umami-rich foods like tomato juice might taste better on a plane.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that umami-rich foods like tomato juice might taste better on a plane

items.text: So, perhaps humans are far more sensory creatures than Aristotle ever imagined.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: far more sensory creatures than Aristotle ever imagined

items.text: From balance and body awareness to the way sound can change flavour, our senses are constantly working together in ways we rarely notice.
